doc.title: Dan Morgenstern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 9, 2013

title: Billie Holiday and the 'buckets of blood' bars
summary: More Harlem scenes: Billie Holiday eating chicken, rough working-class joints like the Locust Club, and Lips welcomed everywhere.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: And at one of the tables, eating some chicken, was Billie Holiday. So I mean Harlem could be, that wasn’t something that happened every night. And there were also places, like Lips knew all these places. There were places that were really like, they called them “buckets of blood,” neighborhood joints frequented by working class people that were pretty rough. I remember one had a turnstile at the bar so that you couldn’t get out before you paid your bill.

That was called the Locust Club. But they had a little bandstand and they had a guy there that was a pretty good tenor player, but he was noted for falling asleep on the bandstand sometimes late in the evening. And Lips was a great jam session guy. You know, that was — he was loved everywhere he went. So if you were with Lips you were welcome anywhere.
